title: Revamp client dependency matrix and sanitize legacy API params
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Consolidate and modernize third-party HTTP and runtime dependencies across Python, JavaScript, and Go SDKs; remove and sanitize legacy API surface fields introduced for older JSON-RPC wrappers. This ticket scopes the coordinated library bump, compatibility shims, test coverage, and migration docs for customers and internal services. Goals: reduce tail latency from transport libs, shrink SDK bundle size for JS, and eliminate surprising behavior caused by legacy params (e.g., 'response_format', 'use_jsonrpc', and 'legacy_streaming').
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK updated to httpx >= 0.24 and asyncio-compatible codepaths validated in unit/integration tests
JS SDK migrated from node-fetch to undici or native fetch where appropriate and bundle size reduced by >= 8% in the browser build
Go SDK deps updated (net/http wrappers removed) and cross-compiled CI matrix passing on amd64/arm64
Deprecated API params ('response_format','use_jsonrpc','legacy_streaming') emit warnings and are removed behind a 90-day compatibility flag
Compatibility shim layer implemented server-side to map legacy params to new surface for 3 months with telemetry indicating usage drop below 0.5% before removal
Release notes and migration guide published with code samples for Python/JS/Go
No regressions in tokenization or streaming observed in canary traffic (latency and error rate within SLOs)
implementation_steps: Audit current transitive deps across SDK monorepo and pin target versions in a central depfile
Prototype Python httpx async transport and run perf microbenchmarks vs requests/urllib3
Create JS experiment with undici + native fetch fallback and measure cold-start/bundle impact
Update Go client to remove internal JSON-RPC shim and rely on direct REST gRPC where applicable
Add feature-flagged compatibility mapping in the gateway to translate legacy params to new fields
Add deprecation warnings in SDKs that are surfaced when legacy params are used
Create integration test matrix (local + ephemeral staging) covering streaming, function calling, and embeddings
Submit PRs for each language client and coordinate cross-language release windows
Coordinate with Console and Dedicated teams for rollout and telemetry collection
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge internal depfile and CI pin changes; run full tests (no user-facing changes)
Week 1: Python/JS/Go experimental branches merged behind feature flags; publish alpha packages and internal quickstart examples
Week 2: Enable server-side shim with telemetry and soft warnings enabled; opt-in canary customers invited
Week 3-6: Monitor telemetry, iterate on edge-case fixes; publish migration guide and deprecation timeline
Week 7: Deprecation flag toggled to enforce warnings for legacy params; communicate to customers via changelog and dashboard
Week 12: If usage falls below threshold, remove shim and ship breaking change in SDKs with final migration helpers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Undetected behavioral diffs in streaming path across runtimes -> Mitigation: end-to-end streaming tests and canary traffic with trace-level logging
Risk: Transitive dependency incompatibilities causing CI flakes -> Mitigation: add hermetic lockfiles and upgrade one major version at a time with compatibility tests
Risk: Customers rely on legacy param semantics -> Mitigation: server-side shim + deprecation warnings + targeted emails to top clients
Risk: Increased binary sizes for Go or JS -> Mitigation: measure bundles and add tree-shaking or replace heavy transitive deps
notes: Related investigation: perf-microbench-2026-01 (internal doc) showed 12% lower p95 using httpx async pool vs requests session under high concurrency
We should avoid a single massive PR. Prefer three language-specific PRs and a small infra PR for the central depfile
Coordinate with security to vet new transitive deps (native bindings) before release
Add a telemetry flag 'legacy_param_usage' to the events schema to track each deprecated field separately
